introduction: 2 Kings records Elijah's departure and Elisha's succession; the Moab war, miracles, and Naaman; the Syrian wars and the siege of Samaria; Jehu's revolution; Athaliah and Joash; the parallel declines of the two kingdoms; the fall of Israel; Hezekiah and the Sennacherib invasion; Manasseh and the sentence on Judah; Josiah's reform and the found book; and the fall of Jerusalem. These eleven studies follow literary divisions; they do not claim eleven independently dated historical events. Archaeology, historical reconstruction, and later interpretation are distinguished from biblical testimony.
